question.problem:
$$ A=[\begin{aligned}5 & -3 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4\end{aligned}],\,y=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]. $$ Given the matrices above, write $A{x}^{T}⊙(y+{x}^{T})$ as a matrix product.
$A{x}^{T}⊙(y+{x}^{T})=\,\,$ {{field-1}} {{field-2}} {{field-3}}
$0$ {{field-4}} $-1$
question.worked_solution:
The Hadamard product of two compatible vectors $u$ and $v$ can be expressed as the matrix product

$$
v⊙u=\text{diag}(v)u.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
A{x}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}5 & -3 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}22 \\ 4\end{aligned}]
$$

and

$$
y+{x}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that they are of the same size; hence, their Hadamard product is well-defined. We conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}A{x}^{T}⊙(y+{x}^{T}) & =\text{diag}(A{x}^{T})(y+{x}^{T}) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}22 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
